title: Equitable strong (vertex-distinguishing) edge colourings: Rudašová–Soták, Theorem 3.1
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 3.1 of J. Rudašová and R. Soták, Vertex-distinguishing proper edge colourings of some regular graphs (Discrete Math. 308, 2008). exists_equitable_strong: if a finite simple graph G has a strong (vertex-distinguishing) proper edge colouring with m colours and m ≤ k, then G has an equitable strong proper edge colouring with k colours. One statement. Edge colourings are colourings of the line graph; the palette of a vertex is the set of colours of its edges; strong means distinct vertices have distinct palettes; equitable means the colour classes differ in size by at most one.
